rationale: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-1 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol): feasibility baseline, NO prior iter. Classical TV-regularized iterative recon (non-trainable) on FBP init over ALL 214 L277 val slices with the 321px detector-geometry FOV. Config = solver defaults (tv_lambda=0.001, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init), conservative tv_iterations=120 sized to fit the HARD 20-min train+score budget across 214 slices (the val recon batches all 214 slices through the 2304-view Mayo geometry in a single autograd graph PER iteration, no chunking; old run timing at val_n=5 gives ~0.018 s/slice-iter -> ~3.9 s/iter at val_n=214 -> 120 iters ~8-9 min incl 214-slice load+FBP+score, ~2x margin). FAILURE MODE TO AVOID: n_iter too high -> 214-slice val pass blows the 20-min wall / OOM. HYPOTHESIS: TV-iterative is structurally bounded by FBP on this real LDCT data, so iter-1 lands near the LD-FBP baseline (hr ~0 to slightly positive); establish the clean datapoint under the corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric.

tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: tv_clip_max 0.05->0.08 (all else held IDENTICAL to iter-1: tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). iter-1 NUMBERS: SSIM 0.922979, hr 0.132941, PSNR 35.32, RMSE 8.57e-4, elapsed 918s (15.3 of 20 min) -- already the best inference solver on Mayo, cleared baseline. FAILURE MODE: the hard upper clamp f.clamp_(0.0, clip_max) at 0.05 truncates every voxel above mu=0.05, i.e. it caps bone / high-attenuation structures; real Mayo LDCT attenuation exceeds 0.05, so bone detail is flattened. The headroom metric is RMSE-sensitive, so the truncated bone is a direct uncredited RMSE penalty. HYPOTHESIS: raising tv_clip_max 0.05->0.08 lets high-mu bone voxels through, so val_ssim and hr rise above iter-1 (0.923 / 0.133), because the 0.05 clamp was the binding upper constraint on bone and the RMSE-sensitive headroom was penalizing its truncation. FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.133 (no gain or regression), the clamp is NOT the binding constraint at this lambda, and iter-3 must instead tune tv_lambda (the data-vs-smoothness balance). BUDGET: tv_clip_max is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- identical iteration count (120) -> identical ~918s wall, ~282s margin under the 1200s 20-min budget preserved. tv_iterations deliberately NOT raised: iter-1 used 918/1200s, so more iters would risk the wall (the failure mode iter-1 flagged). val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged.

column13: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.003, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: tv_lambda 0.001->0.003 (all else held IDENTICAL to iter-2: tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). NUMBERS: iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08) elapsed 928s. Trajectory: the clip bump moved hr +0.072 (0.133->0.205) and dropped RMSE 8.3% by un-truncating high-mu bone -- the clamp WAS the binding constraint (iter-2 falsifier 'hr<=0.133' NOT triggered). iter-2 clip_max=0.08 is now at the TOP of the solver search bound [0.03,0.08] so clip is exhausted as a lever. tv_lambda has been FROZEN at the solver default 0.001 for BOTH prior iters -- never probed -- and is the highest-value untouched knob (the classical data-vs-smoothness balance). FAILURE MODE: Mayo is real LOW-DOSE CT where the dominant error is photon/electronic noise, not under-sampling (2304 views is dense). At lambda=0.001 the data term dominates: SSIM barely moves between iters (recon is data-fit-dominated, leaving the LDCT noise floor in), and the iter-1->2 headroom gain came PURELY from un-truncating bone (clip), NOT from denoising. The regularizer is currently too WEAK to suppress LDCT noise. HYPOTHESIS: raising tv_lambda 0.001->0.003 strengthens the TV denoiser, suppressing residual LDCT noise so val_rmse drops below 7.857e-4 and hr rises above 0.205364; the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower noise floor. 3x is a bounded probe inside [0.0001,0.01] -- large enough to move the needle, small enough not to over-smooth in one shot. FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.205 (no gain or regression) either side of lambda=0.003, TV is AT its regularization ceiling on Mayo (lambda=0.001 was already near-optimal) -- the lever is exhausted and the next probe would be tv_lr/tv_iterations for finer convergence, or accept ~0.92 SSIM / ~0.20 hr as the structural TV ceiling on real Mayo LDCT. BUDGET: tv_lambda is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- identical iteration count (120) -> identical ~928s wall, ~272s margin under the 1200s hard 20-min budget preserved. tv_iterations deliberately NOT raised: iter-2 used 928/1200s, and lambda is the higher-value probe per the mandate. val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged.

tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=160, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). BASE = the iter-2 BEST config (clip 0.08, lambda 0.001), NOT iter-3's regressed lambda 0.003. ONE KNOB: tv_iterations 120->160 (all else held IDENTICAL to iter-2: tv_lambda=0.001, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS): iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05, 120 iters, 918s); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08, 120 iters, 928.5s) -- the BEST, #4 overall on Mayo; iter-3 SSIM 0.919984 hr 0.136636 RMSE 8.536e-4 (lambda 0.001->0.003, 120 iters, 923.9s) -- REGRESSED, over-smoothed (lambda-up is exhausted). The two prior levers are SPENT: tv_clip_max is at the TOP of the solver search bound [0.03,0.08] (clip exhausted), and tv_lambda-up regressed in iter-3 (denoise-strength exhausted). The remaining untried lever is tv_iterations: it has been FROZEN at 120 for all 3 prior iters, deliberately conservative to protect the 20-min wall. OPPORTUNITY: is hr 0.205 ITERATIONS-LIMITED (the TV gradient descent has not fully converged at 120 steps, so the recon still has residual data-term error the schedule has not driven out) or is it at the TV REGULARIZATION CEILING (120 iters is already converged and 0.205 hr / ~0.924 SSIM is the structural TV limit on real Mayo LDCT)? FAILURE MODE TO AVOID: oversizing tv_iterations blows the HARD 20-min (1200s) wall on the 214-slice val pass. HYPOTHESIS: 33% more TV gradient-descent steps (120->160) from the iter-2 BEST config converge the recon further, lowering val_rmse below 7.857e-4 so hr rises above 0.205364 (the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower residual). FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.205 (no gain or regression at 160 iters), TV is at its regularization ceiling on Mayo (~0.924 SSIM / 0.205 hr) and 120 iters was already converged -- the iters lever is exhausted too, and the next probe would be tv_lr (finer convergence per step) or accept the structural TV ceiling. BUDGET: the cost model is T(n)=overhead + n*c_step. From iter-2's 928.5s at 120 iters and the iter-1 per-slice-iter rate (~0.018 s/slice-iter * 214 slices = 3.85 s/TV-iter), fixed overhead (214-slice load+FBP+per-iter scoring) ~= 466s. n=160 -> T ~= 466 + 160*3.85 ~= 1083s = 90% of the 1200s budget (~117s margin). Robustness: even at +10% step-cost variance (GPU contention) n=160 lands ~1144s, still under the wall; n=180 was REJECTED because at +10% variance it goes over (1229s). val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged (do NOT reduce). sbatch --time=00:30:00 gives a SLURM-level safety net above the 20-min metric-validity budget.

tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.02, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-5 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). BASE = the BEST config family (clip 0.08, lambda 0.001) at the BUDGET-PROVEN tv_iterations=120 (NOT iter-4's 160 -- see BUDGET below). ONE KNOB: tv_lr 0.01->0.02 (all else IDENTICAL to the iter-2 BEST: tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS): iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05, 120 iters, 918s); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08, 120 iters, 928.5s) = the BEST, #4 overall on Mayo; iter-3 SSIM 0.919984 hr 0.136636 RMSE 8.536e-4 (lambda 0.001->0.003, 120 iters, 923.9s) REGRESSED (lambda-up exhausted); iter-4 SSIM 0.926664 hr 0.208547 RMSE 7.825e-4 (tv_iterations 120->160, 1227.4s). KEY RECONCILIATION OF THE PLANNED 160->200 KNOB: iter-4's measured elapsed_s was 1227.4s -- already OVER the 1200s HARD 20-min budget at 160 iters -- and 160 iters lifted hr only +0.0031 over the 120-iter iter-2 (0.205364->0.208547), within noise. So tv_iterations 160->200 is INFEASIBLE (cost model fit on the real iter-2/iter-4 pair: c_step=7.47 s/TV-iter, overhead=31.8s => n=200 lands ~1526s = ~25 min, a ~27% overshoot of the wall -> the 214-slice val pass would be killed / the metric invalidated) AND wrong-headed (the iterations lever is already flattening AND budget-capped). FAILURE MODE OBSERVED: the iterations lever has plateaued (120->160 gave +0.003 hr for +33% compute that blew the wall) -- the recon is NOT meaningfully iterations-limited at the cost the budget allows. iter-4's OWN falsifier named the next probe: 'tv_lr (finer convergence per step)'. HYPOTHESIS: doubling the step size (tv_lr 0.01->0.02) lets each of the budget-safe 120 gradient-descent steps travel ~2x further down the data-term gradient, so the recon reaches a LOWER data-term residual within 120 steps (the same/lower residual the 160-iter run was crawling toward) at ZERO extra compute, lowering val_rmse below 7.825e-4 so hr rises above iter-4's 0.208547 -- the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower residual. Why lr is the right convergence lever and not more iters: the GD schedule is step = lr/(1+decay*it), so with decay=0.01 the per-step distance shrinks ~2.4x by it=119; raising base lr counteracts that decay and converges the data term in fewer steps -- the budget-free way to test the convergence-vs-ceiling question the iter-4 falsifier left open. FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.208547 (no gain, or a regression from GD overshoot/oscillation at the larger step), then (a) if hr drops sharply the step is too big and GD overshoots the TV-regularized minimum, and (b) if hr is merely flat then TV is at its REGULARIZATION CEILING on real Mayo LDCT (~0.924 SSIM / ~0.21 hr): 120 iters at lr=0.01 was already converged, the +0.003 from 160 iters was just residual noise, and BOTH the iterations lever (plateaued + budget-capped) AND the step-size lever are exhausted -- accept ~0.21 hr as the structural classical-TV ceiling on this real LDCT substrate and STOP tuning convergence knobs. BUDGET: tv_lr is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- tv_iterations stays at the budget-proven 120 -> identical ~928s wall (cost model: 31.8 + 120*7.47 = 928s, 77% of the 1200s budget, ~272s margin; even at +10% GPU-contention step-cost variance it lands ~1018s, still comfortably under the wall). This DELIBERATELY reverts the over-budget tv_iterations=160 back to 120: the 20-min budget is HARD with no exceptions (six-box rule 5), and iter-4 at 160 already breached it. val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged (do NOT reduce). sbatch --time=00:30:00 gives a SLURM-level safety net above the 20-min metric-validity budget.
